content.text: In countries like Nigeria, where Stripe's [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-minimum-viable-stack|COREMERCH guide to payment]] processing is severely restricted, digital creators rely on workarounds to sell their ebooks, courses, and software. But with Google Apps Script and [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-webhook-driven-crypto-payment-fulfillment-explained-digital-5|cloudflare]] Workers, they can finally automate digital commerce without relying on third-party payment processors like Stripe. By [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/understanding-cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-plain-3|Understanding Cloudflare]] the real architecture behind this infrastructure, creators can build a sovereign digital commerce stack that processes orders in under 30 seconds and handles high volumes of crypto payments with ease.
What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Google apps

Google Apps Script is a cloud-based platform that allows developers to create custom business applications. When used with Cloudflare Workers, it becomes a powerful tool for automating digital commerce workflows. By integrating Apps Script with Cloudflare's global network and NOWPayments' cryptocurrency payment processing, creators can build a sovereign commerce stack that gives them full control over their digital product delivery and payment processing.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture works by using Cloudflare Workers to receive and process webhook events from NOWPayments, which confirms that a crypto payment has been made. Apps Script then uses this information to trigger a custom function that retrieves the digital product from Google Drive and sends it to the customer's email address. This process happens in under 30 seconds, allowing creators to deliver their products quickly and efficiently.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This infrastructure is built for digital creators who rely on Stripe or other third-party payment processors but are facing restrictions or high fees in countries like Nigeria, Ghana, or Kenya. By using Google Apps Script and Cloudflare Workers, these creators can build a sovereign digital commerce stack that allows them to process crypto payments and deliver their products without relying on third-party services.
This infrastructure can process orders in under 30 seconds and handle high volumes of crypto payments with ease.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The key components of this architecture include Google Apps Script, Cloudflare Workers, NOWPayments, and Google Drive. Apps Script provides the custom business logic for processing webhooks and triggering digital product delivery. Cloudflare Workers provides the global network and edge computing capabilities for processing webhooks and handling high volumes of crypto payments. NOWPayments provides the cryptocurrency payment processing and webhook events. Google Drive provides the storage for digital products.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy this infrastructure today, creators can start by setting up their Google Apps Script project and integrating it with Cloudflare Workers. They can then configure NOWPayments to send webhooks to Cloudflare Workers, which will trigger the custom function in Apps Script to deliver the digital product to the customer's email address. This process can be repeated for multiple products and payment gateways.

Your Deployment Checklist

Deploy your backend first — Cloudflare Worker or Google Apps Script Web App — and confirm the endpoint URL is accessible via HTTP POST before configuring NOWPayments. Set the IPN webhook URL in your NOWPayments account settings to point to your backend endpoint. Set the IPN secret key in both NOWPayments and your backend configuration — this is the string that both sides use to verify webhook authenticity. Upload your product files to the configured delivery storage — Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive — with the paths matching your backend configuration. Complete a real mainnet transaction and check your backend logs to confirm the webhook was received, the signature was validated, the transaction was verified on-chain, the order was logged, and the delivery email was sent. Monitor the order database daily for the first week.
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I set up Google Apps Script to receive webhooks from NOWPayments?

To set up Google Apps Script to receive webhooks from NOWPayments, you need to create a project, install the NOWPayments library, and configure the webhook trigger in the Apps Script code. This process can be completed in under 30 minutes.
What happens if the customer's email address is invalid or does not receive the digital product?

If the customer's email address is invalid or does not receive the digital product, the creator can use the Apps Script logs to identify the issue and troubleshoot the problem. This can be done by setting up email delivery using Resend or Gmail and configuring error handling in the Apps Script code.
Can I use this infrastructure to deliver physical products?

No, this infrastructure is designed to deliver digital products only. However, creators can use this infrastructure to deliver digital receipts or invoices for physical products. This can be done by creating a custom function in Apps Script to generate the receipt or invoice and send it to the customer's email address.
How do I handle multiple payment gateways and webhooks?

To handle multiple payment gateways and webhooks, creators can use a library like NOWPayments to manage the webhooks and payment processing. This can be done by installing the library in their Google Apps Script project and configuring the payment gateway and webhook trigger in the Apps Script code.
Can I use this infrastructure to deliver products to customers in different countries?

Yes, this infrastructure can deliver products to customers in different countries. However, creators need to ensure that the digital products are stored in a cloud storage service like Google Drive that has global accessibility and that the email delivery service used is capable of sending emails to customers in different countries.
This architecture is designed to be scalable and flexible, allowing creators to add new payment gateways and webhooks as needed.
